description: Check you actually get why logic lives in the database — executable units, temporary vs resident logic, sequences, and metadata.

questions.explanation: A sequence hands out the next value on every call: 1001, then 1002, then 1003. Never repeats, never skips (in normal use).
Anonymous blocks have no name and aren't stored — running it 'again tomorrow' means retyping it. Resident logic (a stored procedure) is what you call by name later.
options: You can't re-run this by name tomorrow — it's anonymous, not stored
questions.prompt: A student saves this to 'run again tomorrow by name'. What's wrong with the plan?

questions.explanation: Data lives in the database; logic runs closest when it's also in the database (stored units), then anonymous blocks, then app code, then a human typing SQL by hand.
lines: SQL typed by hand in a client
questions.prompt: Arrange from closest to the data (runs inside the DB) to farthest.

questions.code:
CREATE SEQUENCE order_seq START WITH 1001;
-- give me the next order number: ___
questions.explanation: NEXTVAL is the call that asks a sequence for its next value. CURRVAL would give you the current one (the last one handed out in your session).
questions.prompt: Fill in the blank to get the next order number.

questions.code:
-- which of these describes the database itself?
SELECT table_name ___ user_tables;
questions.explanation: user_tables is a data-dictionary view — metadata about the database's own tables. FROM selects from it like any table.
questions.prompt: Fill in the blank to list the database's own tables.

questions.explanation: Procedures act, functions answer, packages organize, sequences number. Four ideas, four jobs.

pairs.definition: Bundle of related procedures and functions
Hands out unique numbers on demand

questions.prompt: Match each database object to its job.

questions.explanation: A procedure performs an action and returns nothing — in Python that's a function with no return value that mutates the data. The option returning a value is function behavior, not procedure behavior.
options: It should be a FUNCTION, not a PROCEDURE
A procedure does an action and returns nothing — that's the whole point
UPDATE can't appear in a procedure
questions.prompt: A student says 'this procedure is broken because it doesn't RETURN anything.' What's wrong with that claim?

questions.explanation: Two columns selected: column_name and data_type. The query describes the table's structure — that's metadata, not the actual order data.
options: All the rows in the ORDERS table
The names and types of ORDERS' columns
An error — you can't query that view

questions.explanation: Same idea, different language: run a bit of logic immediately, no name, nothing stored. Python just runs top-level code the same way.
questions.prompt: Which Python is the same idea — run once, no name, nothing stored?

questions.explanation: Both updates run inside the database in one execution — the logic touches the rows directly, no app round-trips in between. That's the whole point of putting logic next to data.
options: Both updates run inside the database, in one execution
The app fetches both balances first, then updates
Nothing runs until COMMIT is called twice
questions.prompt: Where does the work happen here?
